summary: A one-screen page for Avara, an open-source curveless serif: the name is drawn as an SVG outline with every on-curve point marked by a small purple-stroked handle, framed by a talking headline ('Hello, I am') and a sentence whose emoji are the actions (print the specimen, download, view source). The page prints itself as a specimen sheet through print-only elements.

instances.look: Black screen: 'Hello, I am' in small white serif, then 'Avara' as a huge white SVG outline (~1290px wide) with a small white square handle stroked in violet at every point, showing that the font has only straight segments; a violet outlined circle 'Buy the book!' badge in the top-right corner
instances.ux: The headline talks in the first person; the letterforms are an inline SVG of the glyph paths built with Snap.svg, so the points are scriptable (probably draggable, not confirmed in the capture); a white screen shows for ~1.5s before the page appears
instances.learn: For a font whose idea is its construction (no curves), draw the name as its outline with point handles: the concept is understood before reading a word

reconstruction.layout: Single 100vh screen, centred column: 'Hello, I am' at y≈205; SVG (viewBox -50 -40 900 350) ~1290px wide from x≈76, glyph baseline at y≈620, caps ~390px tall; two-line sentence centred at y≈800–850; 100px circular badge at top-right (≈40px from the edges)
reconstruction.typography: 'Hello, I am' ~36px Avara Bold white; name as SVG paths (fill white, 1px black stroke); sentence ~22px Avara white with inline emoji; badge text ~14px Avara violet, three short lines centred in the circle
reconstruction.behaviour: Static in the capture; <use href=#point-handle> squares (6×6, white fill, stroke rgb(110,50,255)) placed at every path vertex by Snap.svg (js/snap.svg-min.js + pathseg.js polyfill)
reconstruction.content: First-person greeting from the font: 'Hello, I am Avara'
reconstruction.assets: SVG paths of the five glyphs A v a r a
reconstruction.html: div#head.screen; div#svg-container > svg#avara > path ×5 + use[href=#point-handle] per vertex; a.book (badge)

instances.look: One centred sentence under the name: 'you can either 🖨 my specimen, ↓ me, or take a closer 👁.' with the emoji as the links
instances.ux: 🖨 calls window.print() (the page prints as a specimen), ↓ downloads the GitLab master zip, 👁 opens the repository; the word 'specimen' is contenteditable, so the sentence can be retyped
instances.learn: Let the emoji be the verbs in a single sentence: three calls to action with no buttons at all

reconstruction.layout: Centred two-line sentence ~520px wide near the bottom of the screen (y≈800)
reconstruction.typography: ~22px Avara Bold white; emoji at text size
reconstruction.behaviour: a.print-button onclick=window.print(); href to gitlab.com/velvetyne/Avara archive zip and repository; span.editable[contenteditable]
reconstruction.content: you can either 🖨 my specimen, ↓ me, or take a closer 👁.

instances.look: Print-only (HTML only, hidden on screen): when printed, the page adds an alphabet block 'abcdefghijklm / nopqrstuvwxyz / ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ / 1234567890', a block of accents, ligatures (ﬀ ﬁ ﬂ ﬃ ﬄ) and symbols (€ £ Ƀ & ¢ ® © ¶ ½ † ‡), the credit 'Avara Open Source Typeface' and the URL
instances.ux: Appears only through the 🖨 print action (elements with class .print, shown by a print stylesheet)
instances.learn: Hide a character-set sheet in print CSS: the one-screen site becomes a printable specimen with a single window.print()

reconstruction.layout: Two blocks on the printed page: #specimenright (alphabets and figures as four lines) and #specimenleft (accents, punctuation, ligatures, emoji); credits and URL lines
reconstruction.typography: Avara Bold at print display size (exact sizes in main.css, not captured)
reconstruction.content: Alphabet, figures, accented letters, ligatures, symbols
